record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: Let U = ⋃_{α ∈ DC} U_α, where U_α is the class of perturbation potentials whose associated exact symplectic map preserves a smooth invariant torus with Diophantine translation vector α. What is the smallest real number k for which U is open near 0 in the C^k topology?

evidence.quote: Let ⋃α∈DC Uα = U ; what is the minimal number k ∈ R+ for which U is open near 0, in the Ck-topology ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an exact symplectic map on the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ (with its canonical symplectic structure) of the form $F_V = F_0 \circ \Phi_V$, where $F_0(\theta, I) = (\theta + \omega(I), I)$ is an integrable twist map and $\Phi_V$ is the time-one map (or the standard exact-symplectic perturbation) generated by a smooth perturbation potential $V : \mathbb{T}^n \to \mathbb{R}$.

Let $\mathrm{DC} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ denote the set of Diophantine vectors: those $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that there exist constants $\gamma, \tau > 0$ with $|\langle k, \alpha\rangle - m| \geq \gamma |k|^{-\tau}$ for every $k \in \mathbb{Z}^n \setminus \{0\}$ and every $m \in \mathbb{Z}$.

For each $\alpha \in \mathrm{DC}$, let $\mathcal{U}_\alpha$ denote the set of perturbation potentials $V$ for which the associated exact symplectic map $F_V$ admits a smooth invariant Lagrangian torus on which the dynamics is conjugate to the rigid translation $\theta \mapsto \theta + \alpha$. Define
$$\mathcal{U} = \bigcup_{\alpha \in \mathrm{DC}} \mathcal{U}_\alpha.$$

Determine the smallest real number $k \geq 0$ such that $\mathcal{U}$ is a neighborhood of $0$ in the $C^k$ topology on the space of perturbation potentials.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on the minimal regularity threshold for KAM-type openness of the union of Diophantine-frequency invariant-torus classes return general literature on finitely differentiable KAM theorems (Pöschel, de la Llave, and recent positive-measure results in finite differentiability) but no result identifying the exact minimal exponent $k$. The question of the sharp $C^k$ regularity for openness near $0$ appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Tutorial on KAM Theory (de la Llave)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses finite-differentiability versions of KAM and required regularity, without identifying a sharp minimal exponent for openness of the union over Diophantine frequencies.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp minimal regularity for KAM openness is not pinned down in standard tutorials.

status_evidence.title: Positive measure of KAM tori for finitely differentiable Hamiltonians
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishing KAM persistence for finitely differentiable systems, refining regularity thresholds but not resolving the exact minimal $k$ for openness of the union.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results lower regularity bounds but do not give the sharp threshold sought.

status_evidence.title: Classical KAM (Pöschel)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides classical $C^k$ KAM thresholds (e.g., $k > 2n$) but leaves the sharp minimal regularity as an open issue.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference giving sufficient but not necessary regularity.
